newsitem.title: FINLAND: Helsinki bourse ends year 46 pct up, at life high.
newsitem.headline: Helsinki bourse ends year 46 pct up, at life high.

text.p: Finnish shares squeezed a new life high out of an otherwise fairly routine last session of 1996 on Monday, with bourse engine Nokia nudging ahead and some big in-house deals in usually less liquid stocks, brokers said.
With the bourse closed on Tuesday, the general HEX index added 0.56 percent to close at a new life-high of 2,495.93 points, sealing a 46 percent gain for the whole year.
Recent gains on Wall Street and year-end window-dressing played a role as the previous 2,491.99 life-high was surpassed, brokers said. Volume was a thin 350 million markka.
"The same factors continue to boost the market -- low interest rates and the good outlook for share prices," one broker said.
Volume for the year had already hit a new record and he said January and February could be busy if, as expected, money begins to flow out of bank deposits and into equities.
"We're talking hundreds of millions (of markka)," he said, adding that it could add up to billions on the full year level.
Volume for the year towards the end of official hours had surpassed 100 billion markka, bourse officials said, after in November beating its 1995 best of 83 billion markka.

On the day itself one of the highlights was a large inhouse deal of more than 100,000 shares in Asko, made at brokerage Evli. Asko, which later said it was selling a sawmill to state Vapo Oy, had no comment on the trade. Its stock ended down 2.00 markka at 323.00 and was second-busiest on the bourse.
Among other active stocks was Outokumpu, up 0.90 markka at 78.50 with a fair chunk of trades reported after official hours. Finnlines had another lively session, adding 1.00 to 113.00.

Another broker noted that while Helsinki has closed its books for the year, bellwhether Nokia -- which put on 0.90 markka to close at 266.80 and made up about one-third of total volume -- has one day's trade left for its U.S. ADRs.
